slides.say: The average score of the students in a class was seventy. A new student with a score of ninety-four joined the class, and the class average rose to seventy-three. How many students were in the class before the new student joined?
at: The average score of the students

slides.say: So they give two averages and the new student's score. They ask how many students there were before the new student came.
We'll solve it in two different ways. First by understanding, with the balance from the lesson, and then the math way, with an equation.
Like in the lesson, a new score joins, so we compare it to the new average. Ninety-four minus seventy-three is twenty-one. So the new student is twenty-one points above the new average.
The old students had an average of seventy, so each one counts as seventy. Seventy-three minus seventy is three. So each old student is three below the new average.
The twenty-one above must balance the old students below. Each one is three below. Twenty-one divided by three is seven.
So there were seven students before the new student joined.
Careful with eight, choice number three. Eight is the number of students after the new student joined. They ask about before.
at: Eight is the number of students after

slides.say: So seven students, choice number two.
[pause] Now the math way. We start again from the givens. Let's call the number of students before n, and make a table, before and after.
Before, there were n students with an average of seventy. So the sum is seventy n.
at: So the sum is seventy n

slides.say: After, there's one more student, so n plus one students, with an average of seventy-three. So the sum is seventy-three times the bracket, n plus one.
at: So the sum is seventy-three times

slides.say: The new student changes the sum, and also how many students there are. The old sum plus ninety-four is the new sum.
We open the brackets. Seventy-three times the bracket, n plus one is seventy-three n plus seventy-three.
Now we take seventy n and seventy-three away from both sides. Ninety-four minus seventy-three is twenty-one. And seventy-three n minus seventy n is three n.
We divide both sides by three. Twenty-one divided by three is seven, so n is seven.
Seven students before, the same answer. Choice number two is our answer, and I'll see you in the next question.
at: Choice number two is our answer
